messages.content: How much electricity will I need for my 2000 sq ft home?

function.name: solar_panel_calculate_need
function.description: Calculate the number of solar panels needed for a house based on the square footage and average sunlight hours. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

square_footage.description: The square footage of the house. This is a float type value.

average_sunlight_hours.description: The average hours of sunlight received. This is a float type value.

usage_efficiency.description: The efficiency of energy usage in the home, default is 0.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
A good rule‑of‑thumb for a typical U.S. home is **about 5–6 kWh of electricity per square foot per year** (this figure comes from the DOE’s average residential consumption of roughly 10,000–12,000 kWh per year for a 2,000 sq ft house).  

Using that range:

| Metric | Estimate |
|--------|----------|
| **Annual consumption** | 10 000 – 12 000 kWh |
| **Monthly average** | 800 – 1 000 kWh |
| **Daily average** | 25 – 35 kWh |

So for a 2,000 sq ft home you can expect to use roughly **10–12 kWh per square foot per year**, which translates to about **10,000–12,000 kWh per year** overall.

> **Why this matters**  
> • If you’re planning a solar system, you’ll need to size it to meet that annual load.  
> • Your actual usage may be higher or lower depending on climate, insulation, heating/cooling load, appliance efficiency, and lifestyle.  
> • Check your past utility bills for a precise figure—most utilities list total kWh used per month or year.

If you’d like to see how many solar panels you’d need to cover that load, let me know your average sunlight hours and I can run the calculation for you.
